title: Custom ERP — Project Brain
subtitle: Every part of this system, grouped into brain regions, wired by the call graph graphify actually extracted from the source.
_editing: THIS is the file you edit. Everything else in docs/brain/ is generated. To add a region: append to `regions`. To re-file a source file: change a `match` pattern. To re-file one function out of a shared file: add a `symbols` pattern. Then run: graphify update . && go run ./cmd/brainmap

lobes.name: Cortex — Interface
lobes.metaphor: What the user sees and touches. Every business intent enters here.

lobes.name: Brainstem — Kernel
lobes.metaphor: Involuntary and non-negotiable. Every single request passes through here, whatever it is asking for.

lobes.name: Functional Lobes — Business Operations
lobes.metaphor: The specialised areas. Each one owns a domain and can be licensed on its own.

lobes.name: Peripheral Nerves — Integrations
lobes.metaphor: Contact with the outside world: storefronts, payment terminals, marketing clouds, third-party extensions.

lobes.name: Autonomic — Background & Reflexes
lobes.metaphor: Runs without anyone asking it to: outbox drain, pollers, alerting, scheduled sweeps.

lobes.name: Hippocampus — Written Memory
lobes.metaphor: What this project knows about itself: the backlog, the ledger, the guides, the handover note.

lobes.name: Motor Cortex — Build & Delivery
lobes.metaphor: How the system actually moves: build, migrate, promote, back up, restore.

lobes.name: Cerebellum — Verification
lobes.metaphor: Balance and correction. Kept out of the wiring diagrams on purpose — tests touch everything, so drawing them would grey out every real edge.

regions.name: SPA Shell
regions.role: The whole frontend: one hand-written vanilla-JS single-page app, no framework and no build step. Owns routing (renderView), every screen's markup, the two dialog systems, and the shared apiFetch/showApiError error path.

regions.name: Offline Store & Device I/O
regions.role: Browser-side IndexedDB queue that lets POS keep selling when the network drops, plus on-device barcode/QR rendering.

regions.name: Industry Profiles
regions.role: Per-vertical master-data and field packs (jewellery, pharma, food & bev, auto, …) loaded by SwitchIndustryProfile to reshape the same kernel into a different industry.

regions.name: HTTP Edge & Middleware
regions.role: The one door in. apiMiddleware does CORS allowlist, 2MB body cap, per-category rate limiting, panic recovery, JWT verification and tenant resolution, then publishes Resolved-* headers every handler downstream reads. routes.go is the full route table and the background-worker startup list.

regions.name: Error & Message Catalog
regions.role: The 300+ code standard message catalog and the writeAPIError/writeAPIErrorGeneric envelope every handler returns through. Single choke point for what a user is actually told when something fails.

regions.name: Document Kernel
regions.role: The metadata-driven Record Type engine — one generic documents table per tenant plus a doctype_meta/doctype_fields registry. ValidateDocument is the shared validation choke point; document numbering, edit windows and status transitions hang off the same spine.

regions.name: Identity, RBAC & MFA
regions.role: Login, JWT issue/verify, per-role permissions, TOTP MFA for privileged roles, MFA recovery codes and authenticator re-enrollment, account lockout, password reset, and field-level permissions.

regions.name: Tenancy, Packaging & Settings
regions.role: Schema-per-tenant provisioning, the sellable product packages (PIM/WMS/OMS/HR/…) and their module entitlements, tenant limits, the settings registry, and per-tenant UI label overrides.

regions.name: Approval Engine (maker-checker)
regions.role: Amount-banded approval rules, submit → decide → log, bulk decisions, and reset-to-pending when an approved document is edited. Every approval-gated flow in the system routes through this one engine rather than rolling its own.

regions.name: Persistence & Migrations
regions.role: The Postgres connection, GetTenantSchema/SetSearchPath (the tenant boundary, enforced at the SQL layer), the migration runner, and every incremental migration file.

regions.name: Cross-module API Handlers
regions.role: Two historical grab-bag handler files whose contents span several modules (bulk import, availability/checkout, POS sessions, trial balance, approvals, GST, the four core reports, RFQ quotes, stickers, payroll export, the PIM workbench). Kept visible as its own region rather than force-filed under one module, because that is genuinely what they are.

regions.name: Finance & General Ledger
regions.role: Balanced double-entry posting (PostDoubleEntry), chart of accounts, journal vouchers and recurring templates, accounting-period close, cost centres, bank reconciliation, payment proposals and payment files, sales/vendor invoices, debit and credit notes.

regions.name: Tax & Statutory
regions.role: GST computation and enforcement (CGST/SGST/IGST, place-of-supply) and TDS. Called from PO creation, checkout and invoicing rather than living inside any one of them.

regions.name: Procurement & Vendors
regions.role: Purchase Requisition → RFQ and vendor-quote comparison → Purchase Order → GRN → three-way-matched Vendor Invoice → payment, with the requisition catalog and sourcing rules.

regions.name: Inventory & Planning
regions.role: Stock ledger and Available-to-Sell read model (Available − Reserved − Safety Stock − Channel Holds), item lookup by SKU/barcode, location masters, transfer orders, and the replenishment/velocity/demand-forecast engines.

regions.name: Warehouse Management (WMS)
regions.role: Receiving, put-away, slotting, picking, pack counts, 3PL billing, productivity tracking and robotics hooks — the enterprise warehouse tier on top of plain inventory.

regions.name: Orders & Fulfillment (OMS)
regions.role: The order lifecycle: capture, allocation and sourcing, reservation, store/warehouse pick-pack, shipment, and Return Anywhere with RTO/QC/refund.

regions.name: Point of Sale
regions.role: Cart → offer evaluation → GST → tender → GL posting → loyalty accrual, plus cash-drawer sessions, offline heartbeat and session close.

regions.name: Product Information (PIM)
regions.role: Family/attribute framework, taxonomy, approval-gated content with versions and rollback, completeness scoring, media library, bulk edit and CSV round-trip, channel publish queue, and barcode/label printing.

regions.name: CRM & Loyalty
regions.role: Append-only loyalty points ledger with tiering and expiry, redemption security controls, birthday/lapsed-customer campaigns, and customer analytics/reports.

regions.name: HR & Payroll
regions.role: Employee records, attendance and leave, payroll runs and export, and the employee↔user access link.

regions.name: Manufacturing & MRP
regions.role: BOM, production orders (issue → receive), MRP netting, and production scheduling / subcontracting.

regions.name: Fixed Assets
regions.role: Capitalize → straight-line depreciate → transfer → dispose, with the asset register and its GL postings.

regions.name: Expense Management
regions.role: Claim → verify → pay, reusing the approval engine and posting to the GL at payment.

regions.name: Reporting Engine
regions.role: The ReportDefinition/RegisterReport framework, the report registry and column profiles, background exports, and scheduled report delivery. Any new report plugs in here rather than getting its own endpoint.

regions.name: Shipping & Logistics
regions.role: Courier serviceability, logistics booking, shipping labels, manifest generation and handover, and delivery-event tracking.

regions.name: Bulk Data I/O
regions.role: BulkImportCSV — the shared CSV import path (validation, error rows, formula-injection sanitisation) every line-item upload in the system is expected to reuse.

regions.name: Channel Connectors
regions.role: Real Shopify / BigCommerce / Magento API clients, channel credentials encrypted at rest, channel order intake, inbound webhook HMAC verification, plus Unicommerce, Pine Labs and CleverTap integrations.

regions.name: Device Printing (QZ Tray)
regions.role: Silent one-click printing to named OS printers via a QZ Tray bridge on each packing PC. RSA request signing (the tray verifies SHA512withRSA over a SHA-256 hex string), the Printer Master's OS-name/role/language mapping, ZPL/TSPL/ESC-POS command generation, and byte-for-byte pass-through of marketplace-issued label PDFs.

regions.name: Extension Platform
regions.role: Scoped, read-only, HMAC-signed extension tokens, the patch/bug intake worker (which never mutates tenant state by construction), and the standalone third-party SDK contract.

regions.name: Event Outbox
regions.role: The reason a slow third party can never hang a checkout: business writes publish an event into integration_event_outbox inside the same DB transaction, and a background poller drains it afterwards. Retry and integration logs live here too.

regions.name: Logging, Alerting & Notifications
regions.role: Audit log, system error log (a PANIC alerts immediately), the ops alert monitor that watches error rates per tenant schema, user/ops notifications, the ops status surface, and the concurrency scale simulator.

regions.name: Project Documentation
regions.role: The big 3 (micro_checklist / project_ledger / ai_handover) plus the blueprint, guides, SOPs, specs, architecture notes and runbooks. This is where the project stores what it knows about itself between sessions.

regions.name: The Brain Map (this)
regions.role: The map you are reading and the generator that draws it. brain.map.json is the only hand-edited part; BRAIN.md and brain.html are output. Filed as its own region so the brain contains a description of itself, and so a change to the generator shows up in the diagram like any other change.

regions.name: Build, Deploy & Operate
regions.role: manage.ps1 (start/stop/backup/restore/drill), promote.ps1 (worktree → build → migrate → restart, with a red-build gate and rollback), the deploy scripts, CI, and one-shot maintenance commands.

regions.name: Test Suite
regions.role: Every *_test.go in the tree plus the shared test-DB fixture. Deliberately excluded from the wiring diagrams (diagram: false) — tests call into every region, so including them would drown out the real structure.

_declared_links: Connections graphify structurally cannot extract, because they cross a language or process boundary rather than a function call. Asserted here by hand and drawn with a thick ==> arrow so they are never mistaken for measured ones. Add one whenever a real dependency exists that no call graph will ever show.

declared_links.label: HTTP/JSON
declared_links.note: The SPA is JavaScript and the server is Go. apiFetch() calls the route table over the network; no extractor can link the two.

declared_links.label: error envelope
declared_links.note: showApiError() renders the exact code/message the catalog returns. Contract enforced by convention on both sides, invisible to either language's AST.

declared_links.label: queued replay
declared_links.note: Offline POS writes queue into IndexedDB and are replayed against the same endpoints when the network returns.

declared_links.label: loaded at runtime
declared_links.note: SwitchIndustryProfile reads a JSON profile off disk by path; the profiles are data, not code, so nothing links to them statically.

declared_links.label: drains the queue
declared_links.note: The outbox worker dispatches by event name through a registry rather than by direct call, so the edge is a table lookup, not a call site.

declared_links.label: applies migrations
declared_links.note: promote.ps1 and deploy/migrate.sh run the migration files; PowerShell and .sql are both outside the Go call graph.

declared_links.label: builds & restarts
declared_links.note: manage.ps1/promote.ps1 build the binary and control its lifecycle from outside the process entirely.

declared_links.label: keeps in sync
declared_links.note: The brain is regenerated alongside the big 3 docs; the relationship is a convention in CLAUDE.md, not a code dependency.

pathways.name: Request signal path
pathways.note: What happens to one API call, in order. Everything downstream of apiMiddleware trusts the Resolved-* headers it sets and nothing the client claimed.

steps.label: apiMiddleware: CORS → 2MB cap → rate limit → panic recovery
JWT verify → tenant resolve → Resolved-Tenant-ID / Resolved-User-ID headers

pathways.name: Outbound integration path
pathways.note: No user-facing transaction ever makes a synchronous outbound HTTP call. This is why a down Shopify cannot hang a checkout.

pathways.name: Maker-checker path
pathways.note: Any approval-gated document follows this. Editing an already-approved document resets it to pending rather than silently keeping the approval.

pathways.name: Boot & reflex startup
pathways.note: What comes up when the binary starts, before it ever serves a request. One cancellable context is threaded into every worker so SIGTERM lets them finish a tick and exit.

steps.label: background workers: outbox, PIM publish, Magento poll, patch intake, ops alerts, integrations, report export, scheduled reports, recurring journals, loyalty expiry, campaigns
